newsitem.title: GERMANY: Three women killed in German church bombing.
newsitem.headline: Three women killed in German church bombing.

text.p: Three women were killed and 10 people, including a 12-year-old girl, were seriously injured in a Christmas Eve bomb attack in a crowded Frankfurt church, German police said on Wednesday.
The powerful bomb blew one victim to pieces. Police said the dead woman was considered the primary suspect in the attack that horrified the nation in the midst of Christmas celebrations.
Two women sitting next to her near the back of the small Protestant church were also killed by the blast, which shook the Frankfurt district of Sindlingen shortly before midnight.

"We suspect this woman blew herself up, but we do not know anything about her motives," said police spokesman Manfred Feist. "We can only speculate about the motives. Perhaps this was an emotionally disturbed person."
He said there were no advance warnings of any kind. One police official said the bomb appeared to be a "home-made job".

A witness told police there had been a "muffled bang" at the rear of the church, which was packed with about 70 worshippers for a Christmas service. Authorities said panic broke out as people ran for the doors.
"I have no idea who could have done such a thing on a day like this," Frankfurt police chief Wolfhard Hoffmann told reporters at the scene. "We are completely baffled."
Police said preliminary investigations suggested the attack was not the work of guerrillas.
"We have largely ruled out this being a terrorist attack," said Feist.
The bomb exploded at about 11.15 p.m. (2215 GMT) on Tuesday night.
Small bits of blood-covered human flesh and pieces of splintered wood from wrecked pews were scattered throughout the back of the church.
Emergency workers were still carrying pieces of bodies out of the church in plastic bags hours after the attack.

There did not appear to be any foreigners in the church or among the casualties. Sindlingen is a working class area of Frankfurt, Germany's financial centre. It is near the sprawling Hoechst AG chemical plant.
Sirens from dozens of ambulances, police cars and fire engines pierced the late night silence of the city. Streets were nearly empty because of the Christmas holiday.
Besides the three dead and 10 seriously injured, three people were slightly injured and many others were treated for shock.
Police said the bomb was placed in the third row of pews from the back of the church.

At first police said they were searching for a woman they considered a suspect because witnesses reported seeing her near the church with her face partially covered by a scarf. But that theory was later discarded, partly because temperatures were well below freezing and many people were wearing scarfs.
Police later said they suspected the bomber was one of the victims -- a woman who had entered the service late.
Her body was torn to shreds by the bomb. But police said the suspect's head, although severed from the body, had not been disfigured.
They said they planned to photograph the face and distribute copies to the media in hopes of obtaining clues from the public.
"We hope to receive information about her identity and learn further details that could help resolve the attack," said a police officer.
One of the other victims survived the blast but died while still in the church as she was being treated by a doctor, police said.
Police quickly sealed off the area around the church and officers in the entire Frankfurt region were put on high alert.
